summary.intent: Drive a multi-agent wave of work on the monokl repo: fix analyzer default-export classification, speed up the match path, refresh core-types docs, then tackle the next bottleneck (dedup_blocks) the perf agent identified.
summary.outcome: Three PRs were opened (#73 default-export kind fix, #74 rayon parallelization of text search and block retrieval, #72 core-types docs), and a dedup_blocks per-file optimization agent was started. Full CI on the PRs was not yet confirmed, and the dedup result was not yet reported.

repo: Analyzer block kinds carry ranking weights: Other is 0.7 and Function is 1.5, so a misclassified kind directly lowers file/block rank (e.g. axios buildFullPath and dispatchRequest ranked below where they should).
Quality gate is scripts/rg-compare.py (run with python3 -I) with thresholds such as member questions >= 90% (currently 15/16 = 93.75%); `just ci` is the main local check.
Changes to the monokl crate need a changeset file in .changeset/ (patch for fixes/perf); docs-only changes do not.
rayon was workspace-only and had to be added as a dependency of the monokl crate for #74.
Output determinism matters: file ceiling, diagnostics and output order depend on walk order, so parallel work must fold results in walk order (ignore's build_parallel was rejected for this reason).
dedup_blocks (src/dedup.rs) takes about 30 of 51 ms on broad queries (1678 candidates for zod 'string optional') and is now the dominant cost.
Entire Gates check on each PR waits on user approval, and the PRs have a merge order: #70, #71, then #72-#74 in any order.

code.finding: statement_kind lacked an arm for ExportDefaultDeclaration, so it fell to Other; the fix maps Function/Class/Interface declarations to their kinds and leaves expressions and specifiers as Other.
Agent output prints the parent as a column formatted '<kind> <name>'.

dedup_blocks is the remaining hot spot; the optimization compares each candidate only against overlapping kept blocks in its own file, gated by byte-identical output and the existing reference proptest in dedup/proptests.rs.

workflow: Verify subagent claims independently by checking CI exit codes rather than trusting reported summaries; the assistant noted CI was still pending on all three PRs.
Profile before optimizing: the perf agent measured stage costs (text search ~18 ms, retrieve ~18 ms, rank ~4 ms) and declined a third change when the remaining cost sat in an out-of-scope file.
Validate perf refactors with large old/new differential runs (99 runs of stdout, stderr and exit code across 33 queries, 3 flag sets and 3 repos) and medians over 25 runs.
Write tests that fail before the fix and replace tests that pinned wrong behavior.
Agents scoped to allowed files should report out-of-scope findings (dedup) to be handled by a separate agent.

friction: The dedup bottleneck was in src/dedup.rs, outside the perf agent's allowed files, so it could not be fixed in the same pass.
Benchmarks ran on a loaded machine (load avg 11-23), which adds noise to timing numbers.
Entire Gates on each PR is failing or pending until the user approves, blocking merges.
CI for the three PRs had not finished at the time of the summary, so none could be confirmed fully green.
open_items: Confirm full CI results by exit code on PRs #72, #73 and #74, and approve Entire Gates.
Review and verify the dedup_blocks optimization (changeset, dedup.rs, proptests.rs) once the agent reports back.
Text search now holds all per-file hits before applying the file ceiling, so memory can grow on pathological queries matching over 100k files.
Decide whether a default-exported arrow or function expression should rank as Function; the harness shows no need yet.
Docs PR #72 was not validated with just ci or rg-compare.py locally.
Per-file parse thread spawn in analysis/** was not measured or changed.
